guide.summary: Lets a grazer coat itself in a thin mineral jacket that makes it slower to catch but also slower to move.
guide.biology: Some real single-celled organisms build coats from minerals they collect from the water around them.
guide.rules: Costs 0.02 energy per second while carried. Builds a jacket from local free silicate toward 0.10 mineral per unit of body, at up to 0.005 × starting body per second, paying 10 energy per mineral bound. No building while resting, held, below 15 energy or dead. Coverage c is the jacket divided by its target, from 0 to 1. Speed is multiplied by (1 − 0.20c), and Needlejaw needs 1 + 3c seconds of contact to capture it instead of 1. It grants no immunity and no other protection. Division splits the jacket; a daughter without the module drops hers as grit.
guide.example: Add silicate to a dish with Needlejaws and compare how long jacketed and plain Amoebas last.
